prompt: In a dig response's ANSWER SECTION showing `example.com. 86400 IN A 93.184.215.14`, what does the 86400 represent?
choices: The port number the record applies to
The TTL in seconds -- how long the record can be cached
The record's priority relative to other A records
The timestamp the record was created, in Unix epoch seconds

prompt: A server runs nginx on port 80 and Postgres on port 5432 at the same IP address. What actually lets the kernel deliver incoming packets to the correct process?
choices: The destination port number, as part of the connection's 4-tuple
The order in which the processes were started
A separate IP address assigned internally to each process
The HTTP Host header in the request

prompt: In a raw HTTP/1.1 request sent over a TCP connection, what signals the end of the headers and the start of the body (or end of the request)?
choices: A line containing only the word END
The Content-Length header reaching zero
A blank line (\r\n\r\n after the last header)
The TCP connection being closed by the client

prompt: Why is the Host header required in an HTTP/1.1 request even though the client already connected to a specific IP address?
choices: It encrypts the request so intermediate routers cannot read the path
It lets one IP/port serve multiple domains (virtual hosting), so the server knows which site is being requested
It specifies which port on the server to use
It is only used for HTTPS, not plain HTTP

prompt: A Flask app bound with `app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=5000)` responds to curl from inside the VM it's running on, but every curl from an external machine times out. What's the direct cause?
choices: The cloud provider's DNS has not propagated yet
127.0.0.1 is the loopback interface, which only accepts connections originating from the same machine
Port 5000 is a reserved port that cloud providers block by default
Flask's development server cannot handle more than one client at a time

prompt: After fixing the bind address to 0.0.0.0, external curl requests still time out. What is the most likely remaining cause specific to cloud VMs?
choices: The private key was not regenerated after the code change
The app needs to be restarted with sudo
A firewall or cloud security-group rule is not allowing inbound traffic on that port
0.0.0.0 only works for HTTPS traffic, not plain HTTP

prompt: Running `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` produces id_ed25519 and id_ed25519.pub. Which statement about these two files is correct?
choices: Both files must be copied to the remote server's authorized_keys
id_ed25519.pub is safe to share and gets placed in the remote server's authorized_keys; id_ed25519 must stay private and never leave your machine
id_ed25519 is uploaded to the server; id_ed25519.pub stays local
The two files are interchangeable copies of the same key for redundancy

prompt: You need to download a 27 MB installer archive onto a remote server and you don't need to inspect headers or script anything else around it. Which tool is the more direct fit?
choices: curl, because wget cannot handle HTTPS
wget, because it is built for saving a URL's contents to disk by default
dig, because it resolves the download URL first
nc (netcat), because it works at the TCP level
